subject: Clarify: what counts as stored artifacts (prompts, embeddings, KV cache)
messages:
From: Elena Morales <security@finpayments.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Quick question on what Redwood stores by default (prompts/outputs/derivatives)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — we liked the latency profile. Before we proceed I'd like one crisp answer for our security review: by default for the hosted API, does Redwood retain the following items beyond immediate processing?
- Raw prompts (full user messages)
- Model outputs (generated text)
- Derivatives such as embeddings and reranker scores
- Any ephemeral model state (KV cache snapshots or similar)

If any of these are retained, what is the default retention period and where (which region)? Also, what is the deletion workflow for a discovery/legal request — will a single API call wipe historical stored artifacts for a project?

Appreciate a short, actionable summary and any attachments you can share for our audit team.

Best,
Elena Morales
Head of Security Operations
FinPayments

Attachment: SOC2-request-template.docx (referenced)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on what Redwood stores by default (prompts/outputs/derivatives)

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Pushing a concise answer from product/engineering + legal below; attaching our short retention summary and a SOC2 note we use with prospects.

Short summary (high level):
- Prompts and model outputs: by default the hosted API retains request/response artifacts for 30 days for troubleshooting, billing, and quality monitoring. This includes text prompts and generated outputs unless a customer has enabled request redaction or is on a Dedicated/Private deployment.
- Derivatives (embeddings, reranker scores): treated as derived artifacts — retained by default for 30 days as well. We treat embeddings the same as outputs for retention purposes.
- Ephemeral model state (KV cache, in-memory weights): not persisted long-term. Any KV cache state used during inference is ephemeral per request and not written to persistent logs.

Deletion and workflows: we provide a deletion API and support ticket path to remove stored artifacts earlier than the default TTL. For enterprise customers we can scope deletions to project/environment and produce a deletion report. See the attached "retention-summary-2026-11-30.pdf".

Karthik / Lauren — flagged for any additional technical/legal nuance (esp. embeddings and whether derived vector DBs created by customers via the API are in-scope).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments: retention-summary-2026-11-30.pdf (PDF), SOC2-answers-FinPayments.pdf (PDF)

Subject: Re: Quick question on what Redwood stores by default (prompts/outputs/derivatives)

Hi Elena — short technical clarifications to supplement Marissa's note: entirely focused on hosted API defaults (Dedicated/Private differ as noted).

1) Prompts / Outputs:
- What we persist: request metadata (timestamps, model id, route), the request body (prompts) and the response body (outputs) are stored in our telemetry store for 30 days by default. This supports debugging, billing reconciliation, and quality monitoring.
- Redaction: customers can opt to redact parts of the prompt at the client or server-side; server-side redaction removes fields before persistence. Redaction is not retroactive (it applies to new requests once enabled).

2) Embeddings & Derivatives:
- If you generate embeddings via the embeddings endpoint, those vectors are treated as outputs and are retained under the same 30‑day TTL. If you export embeddings to your own vector DB (customer-managed), those copies are out of scope for Redwood retention unless we ingest them back into Redwood services.
- Reranker scores and internal scorer outputs are stored as part of the model output payload.

3) KV cache / model internal state:
- We do not write KV cache states to persistent logs. A transient KV cache exists in serving memory per session to accelerate autoregressive decoding; it's not persisted beyond the request lifecycle.

4) Deletion API & scoped deletion:
- We support an authenticated deletion endpoint (DELETE /v1/projects/{id}/artifacts) that accepts filters (date range, route, request-id list) and returns a job id. Deletion is eventual-consistent — artifacts are removed from primary indexes within 24 hours and background indexes/backup snapshots are pruned within 7–30 days depending on legal/backup retention.
- For enterprise accounts (like FinPayments) we offer a certified deletion report and can contract shorter backup windows.

If you want, we can provide a short runbook for your legal team that maps retention states to compliance controls (I can draft).

-Karthik
Principal Engineer, Inference Runtime
karthik@redwood.com
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Quick question on what Redwood stores by default (prompts/outputs/derivatives)

Elena — welcome follow-up from legal perspective. A few contract and process notes: 

- Contract position: our standard hosted terms state a 30-day default retention for request/response logs used for operating the service and improving model quality unless a customer requests otherwise and we amend scope in the SOW. For Dedicated/Private deployments data residency and retention are governed by the customer's environment and our deployment agreement.

- Deletion requests: we process verified deletion requests via our support portal. For PCI/regulated customers we require an ATO or POA validation flow; once validated we schedule the deletion job and provide a tokenized deletion report. Expect turnaround 2–5 business days for scoped deletes; for full-account certified deletion we coordinate a programmatic run and provide evidence (may require additional contractual terms).

- Embeddings nuance: if FinPayments relies on Redwood to both generate and host embeddings (e.g., using our vector search addon), we will include those in deletion unless the customer has exported vectors out-of-band. If you self-host vectors, that data is outside Redwood's retention scope — include that detail in your audit notes.

I'll follow up with a short redlined paragraph you can drop into your security questionnaire.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
lauren@redwood.com
